messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechco.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the candid discussion on expected load and performance targets. Per our demo, I wanted to capture the performance/SLO items we discussed and propose concrete next steps so we can align the benchmark and MAP (mutual action plan).

Summary of what I captured during the call:
- P95 latency target for single-turn requests (avg payload ~512 tokens): <= 200ms
- Streaming requirement: first-byte latency <= 120ms and steady token emission suitable for low-latency UI streaming
- Sustained throughput: ~500 QPS for classification/generation endpoints (bursty up to 1,000 QPS for 2–3 min windows)
- Expected concurrent requests during peak: ~200 concurrent inference sessions (mix of single-turn and streaming)
- Model size: customer evaluating 7B–13B family; prefer quantized/latency-optimized variant if it meets quality bar

Proposed next steps (we can run these in parallel):
1) Redwood runs a focused benchmark with a representative payload and both single-turn and streaming scenarios (we'll run on dedicated hardware matching your target region).
2) Customer provides a representative sample payload set + expected sequence length distribution and tokenization guidance (this helps with kernel selection and batching).
3) Agree on concrete acceptance criteria (p95, p99, first-byte streaming, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens) and sign off on MAP timelines.
4) Draft a scoped SOW/benchmark plan and schedule a 2-hour joint run next week.

Can you confirm the numbers above and share the sample payloads (anonymized is fine)? Once we have that, Aditya will schedule the benchmark and share a proposed test matrix.

I'll follow up with the SLO checklist and proposed MAP items.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — this matches our notes. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side:

- P95 target: yes, <= 200ms for typical single-turn requests (median payload ~350 tokens; 95th around 512 tokens). For longer documents (1–2k tokens) we expect a relaxed SLA but would like to see tail behavior.
- Streaming: first-byte <= 120ms is what our UX team needs; sustained token emission at ~15–20 tokens/sec is a good baseline for the streaming UI.
- Throughput: 500 QPS sustained is our planning target. We do expect spikes up to 1,000 QPS for up to 3 minutes during peak trading alerts; graceful degradation is fine if we understand fallback behavior.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent sessions is correct; distribution skews toward many short-lived requests with periodic long-lived streaming sessions.

We can provide a sample payload set (anonymized) — I'll attach a ZIP to a follow-up email if that works. Also keen to get a cost estimate for the two benchmarked model variants (7B quantized and 13B q4) so we can line that up with procurement.

One question: can Redwood run both single-turn and streaming tests in the same benchmark run, or should those be separate?

Cheers,
Samir
Head of Product, FintechCo
Samir.Shah@fintechco.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechco.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: FintechCo performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Marissa / team —

Happy to run the benchmark. A couple of engineering clarifications that will let us size the tests and produce actionable results:

1) Please confirm tokenization and average sequence length distribution (Samir mentioned median ~350, 95th ~512; please provide a small sample).
2) For streaming, confirm target first-byte and sustained tokens/sec (Samir called out first-byte <= 120ms, 15–20 tokens/sec). We'll need to emulate client-side backpressure to match UX patterns.
3) Concurrency profile: what percent of concurrency is streaming vs single-turn? e.g., 80% short single-turn, 20% streaming long-lived sessions.
4) Payload size/batchability: are requests typically single prompt or batched across users? Higher batchability changes kernel selection and batching windows.
5) Tolerance for quantization tradeoffs: do you require bit-exact parity vs baseline, or is a small delta in quality acceptable for the 7B q4 path?

Benchmark plan (high level):
- Run single-turn latency tests across 7B-q4 and 13B-q4 variants at sequence lengths: 128, 350, 512, 1024 (tail). Compute p50/p95/p99 and 95th for token emission in streaming.
- Run sustained throughput tests at 100/250/500/1000 QPS with realistic inter-arrival patterns; measure CPU/GPU utilization and KV-cache hit behavior.
- Run concurrency stress with mixed streaming/single-turn profile (we recommend starting at 50% streaming / 50% single-turn for initial runs unless customer specifies otherwise).
- Provide a short report with SLO pass/fail and suggested config knobs (batching window, max_batch_size, quantization profile) and an estimated cost-per-1M tokens at observed throughput.

Attaching the SLO checklist we'll use as the formal artifact for the MAP — please review and flag any additional acceptance criteria.

Attachments: fintechco-slo-checklist.pdf (SLO checklist & test matrix)

I'll schedule time next week once Samir confirms payloads and preferred test window.

—Aditya
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
